answer.rationale: The degradation is confined to the primary region and correlates temporally with a release deployed 2 hours ago. Write-path p99 at 5x target during peak settlement traffic suggests a regression introduced by the new build rather than a capacity or infrastructure issue. Memory_b1 (day 18) documents an analogous situation where a rollback cleared a checkout error spike with no customer impact and the prior build was stable. A regional failover would protect availability but would also disrupt in-flight settlement writes at peak load; adding capacity addresses throughput, not a code-level regression; circuit breakers and read-replica routing do not target the write path. Rolling back to the prior stable build is the single intervention most likely to restore write-path latency while preserving customer writes through the settlement peak.
